title: T1110: Brute Force - Description
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1110 (Brute Force)
Tactics: Credential Access
Description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained. Without knowledge of the password for an account or set of accounts, an adversary may systematically guess the password using a repetitive or automated process.

title: T1110: Brute Force - Detection Guidance
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1110 (Brute Force) Detection Guidance
Tactics: Credential Access
Detection Strategy: Monitor authentication logs for repeated failed login attempts from a single source IP or targeting specific accounts within a short time window. Correlate with event sources like /var/log/auth.log, Linux auditd, Windows Security Event ID 4625, and VPN gateway logs.

title: T1110: Brute Force - Mitigation Controls
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1110 (Brute Force) Mitigation Controls
Tactics: Credential Access
Mitigation & Defenses: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) across all remote access services. Enforce rate limiting and automated IP banning (e.g., fail2ban) after consecutive authentication failures. Enforce account lockout thresholds.

title: T1110.001: Password Guessing - Description
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1110.001 (Password Guessing)
Tactics: Credential Access
Description: Adversaries may guess passwords to gain access to accounts. Password guessing attempts systematically cycle through common or default passwords against targeted known accounts, such as administrator, root, oracle, or test. This attack typically generates multiple failed authentication events on a single or small set of accounts.

title: T1110.001: Password Guessing - Detection Guidance
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1110.001 (Password Guessing) Detection Guidance
Tactics: Credential Access
Detection Strategy: In OpenSSH logs, look for repeated 'Failed password for root' or 'Failed password for invalid user' log messages originating from external IP addresses. A sudden spike in failed authentication volume followed by a successful login indicates potential compromise.

title: T1110.001: Password Guessing - Mitigation Controls
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1110.001 (Password Guessing) Mitigation Controls
Tactics: Credential Access
Mitigation & Defenses: Disable direct root login over SSH (PermitRootLogin no). Enforce strong password complexity requirements. Require cryptographic key-based authentication and disable password-based SSH access entirely.

title: T1110.003: Password Spraying - Description
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1110.003 (Password Spraying)
Tactics: Credential Access
Description: Adversaries may use password spraying to attempt a single or small set of common passwords across a large number of distinct user accounts to avoid account lockouts. This technique avoids triggering traditional brute-force detection rules that look for repeated failures on a single user.

title: T1110.003: Password Spraying - Detection Guidance
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1110.003 (Password Spraying) Detection Guidance
Tactics: Credential Access
Detection Strategy: Monitor for single source IP addresses or clusters of distributed IPs attempting logins across multiple distinct usernames in quick succession. Look for high ratios of unique usernames per source IP address in authentication telemetry.

title: T1110.003: Password Spraying - Mitigation Controls
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1110.003 (Password Spraying) Mitigation Controls
Tactics: Credential Access
Mitigation & Defenses: Deploy CAPTCHA or proof-of-work challenges on public authentication endpoints. Implement continuous anomaly detection monitoring authentication velocity across the entire directory service.

title: T1078: Valid Accounts - Description
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1078 (Valid Accounts)
Tactics: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
Description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing, legitimate accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Compromised credentials can be obtained through brute-force attacks, credential dumping, or purchasing credentials on dark web forums.

title: T1078: Valid Accounts - Detection Guidance
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1078 (Valid Accounts) Detection Guidance
Tactics: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
Detection Strategy: Investigate authentication sequences where multiple failed attempts are followed by a successful login. Analyze anomalous login locations, unexpected time-of-day logins, unusual user-agent strings, and concurrent active sessions for the same user.

title: T1078: Valid Accounts - Mitigation Controls
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1078 (Valid Accounts) Mitigation Controls
Tactics: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
Mitigation & Defenses: Enforce conditional access policies that restrict logins based on geographic anomaly or device compliance. Require hardware security keys or FIDO2 MFA. Audit account usage and immediately revoke credentials upon detection of compromise.

title: T1087.001: Account Discovery: Local Accounts - Description
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1087.001 (Account Discovery: Local Accounts)
Tactics: Discovery
Description: Adversaries may attempt to obtain a listing of local system accounts to understand what users exist on the host and identify high-privilege administrative accounts for subsequent targeting.

title: T1087.001: Account Discovery: Local Accounts - Detection Guidance
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1087.001 (Account Discovery: Local Accounts) Detection Guidance
Tactics: Discovery
Detection Strategy: Look for authentication logs attempting to connect using non-existent usernames ('invalid user' messages in sshd). On endpoints, monitor execution of commands such as 'cat /etc/passwd', 'getent passwd', 'net user', or 'whoami'.

title: T1087.001: Account Discovery: Local Accounts - Mitigation Controls
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1087.001 (Account Discovery: Local Accounts) Mitigation Controls
Tactics: Discovery
Mitigation & Defenses: Restrict read access to sensitive user configuration files where possible. Limit verbose error messages on public login banners that reveal whether a username is valid or invalid.

title: T1021.004: Remote Services: SSH - Description
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1021.004 (Remote Services: SSH)
Tactics: Lateral Movement
Description: Adversaries may log in into remote machines using Secure Shell (SSH) with valid credentials or stolen SSH private keys. Once authenticated, adversaries can execute remote commands, pivot to internal networks, and establish persistent reverse tunnels.

title: T1021.004: Remote Services: SSH - Detection Guidance
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1021.004 (Remote Services: SSH) Detection Guidance
Tactics: Lateral Movement
Detection Strategy: Audit SSH session openings (pam_unix session opened) and correlate with known administrative jumpboxes. Flag direct SSH connections originating from unexpected external IP subnets or non-standard client software.

title: T1021.004: Remote Services: SSH - Mitigation Controls
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1021.004 (Remote Services: SSH) Mitigation Controls
Tactics: Lateral Movement
Mitigation & Defenses: Restrict SSH ingress at perimeter firewalls to authorized VPN or bastion hosts. Restrict SSH listening ports or bind sshd strictly to private management interfaces. Enforce SSH host key verification.

title: T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Description
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1059 (Command and Scripting Interpreter)
Tactics: Execution
Description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters (such as Bash, sh, Python, PowerShell) to execute arbitrary commands, download secondary payloads, and automate intrusion workflows.

title: T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Detection Guidance
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1059 (Command and Scripting Interpreter) Detection Guidance
Tactics: Execution
Detection Strategy: Monitor process creation events (auditd Syscall 59 / Windows 4688) for interactive shells spawned directly by sshd or web server worker processes. Look for suspicious command lines involving curl, wget, base64 decoding, or reverse shell syntax.

title: T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter - Mitigation Controls
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1059 (Command and Scripting Interpreter) Mitigation Controls
Tactics: Execution
Mitigation & Defenses: Enforce application allowlisting. Restrict non-administrative users from executing administrative shells. Enable script block logging and auditd process tracing.

title: T1496: Resource Hijacking - Description
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1496 (Resource Hijacking)
Tactics: Impact
Description: Adversaries may leverage the resources of co-opted systems in order to solve resource-intensive problems, most commonly unauthorized cryptocurrency mining (cryptojacking).

title: T1496: Resource Hijacking - Detection Guidance
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1496 (Resource Hijacking) Detection Guidance
Tactics: Impact
Detection Strategy: Observe sustained 100% CPU utilization across all cores, outbound network connections to known mining pool endpoints (stratum+tcp), and process names imitating legitimate daemons (e.g., kworker, systemd-udev).

title: T1496: Resource Hijacking - Mitigation Controls
text:
MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1496 (Resource Hijacking) Mitigation Controls
Tactics: Impact
Mitigation & Defenses: Set resource quotas (cgroups) for unprivileged service accounts. Block outbound traffic to known cryptocurrency mining domain lists and pool ports.

title: IR-PLAYBOOK-001: SSH Brute-Force & Password Guessing Incident Response Playbook - Investigation Steps
text:
Incident Response Playbook: SSH Brute-Force & Password Guessing Incident Response Playbook (IR-PLAYBOOK-001)
NIST Phase: Triage & Containment | Category: Credential Access
Summary: Standard operating procedure for investigating and containing high-volume automated SSH authentication failure bursts.
Investigation Steps:
1. Verify the originating IP address in external threat intelligence databases (AbuseIPDB, VirusTotal).
2. Calculate failure rate and total duration of the authentication burst.
3. Inspect whether any targeted accounts are valid local users versus non-existent accounts.
4. Verify whether any authentication attempt from the attacker IP resulted in a successful session (Accepted password/publickey).
5. Inspect other hosts in the enterprise network to determine if the same source IP is targeting other exposed services.
Reference: NIST Special Publication 800-61 Revision 2: Computer Security Incident Handling Guide, Section 3.2

title: IR-PLAYBOOK-001: SSH Brute-Force & Password Guessing Incident Response Playbook - Containment & Remediation
text:
Incident Response Playbook: SSH Brute-Force & Password Guessing Incident Response Playbook (IR-PLAYBOOK-001) - Remediation Controls
Containment Actions:
1. Implement temporary or permanent drop rule for originating IP on perimeter firewall (iptables / AWS Security Group).
2. Ensure fail2ban or dynamic rate-limiting service is functioning on the targeted host.
3. If legitimate accounts were targeted, notify account owners and review recent activity.

Remediation Actions:
1. Disable password-based SSH authentication in /etc/ssh/sshd_config (PasswordAuthentication no).
2. Require SSH keys with passphrase protection and hardware tokens (FIDO2).
3. Restrict SSH access to authorized VPN gateways or bastion jump hosts.
Reference: NIST Special Publication 800-61 Revision 2: Computer Security Incident Handling Guide, Section 3.2

title: IR-PLAYBOOK-002: Compromised Valid Account & Unauthorized Access Playbook - Investigation Steps
text:
Incident Response Playbook: Compromised Valid Account & Unauthorized Access Playbook (IR-PLAYBOOK-002)
NIST Phase: Eradication & Recovery | Category: Initial Access / Privilege Escalation
Summary: Emergency playbook for situations where repeated authentication failures precede an accepted login session.
Investigation Steps:
1. Immediately isolate the affected host from the internal network while preserving volatile memory (RAM).
2. Determine exact timestamp of the successful login (pam_unix session opened).
3. Audit all commands executed during the session via shell history (.bash_history), auditd logs, or process creation events.
4. Check for persistence mechanisms added during session: new cron jobs, modified ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, new sudoers entries, or newly created accounts.
5. Identify any outbound network connections initiated by the user session (potential reverse shells or data staging).
Reference: NIST Special Publication 800-61 Revision 2, Section 3.3 (Containment, Eradication, and Recovery)

title: IR-PLAYBOOK-002: Compromised Valid Account & Unauthorized Access Playbook - Containment & Remediation
text:
Incident Response Playbook: Compromised Valid Account & Unauthorized Access Playbook (IR-PLAYBOOK-002) - Remediation Controls
Containment Actions:
1. Terminate all active SSH sessions and processes belonging to the compromised user account.
2. Lock the user account immediately (usermod -L <username>).
3. Revoke all active session tokens, Kerberos tickets, and SSH authorized keys for the account.

Remediation Actions:
1. Force credential reset and re-enrollment of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
2. Re-image or restore the compromised host from a known clean backup if root privileges were attained.
3. Audit surrounding systems accessible with the compromised credentials.
Reference: NIST Special Publication 800-61 Revision 2, Section 3.3 (Containment, Eradication, and Recovery)

title: IR-PLAYBOOK-003: User Enumeration & Account Reconnaissance Playbook - Investigation Steps
text:
Incident Response Playbook: User Enumeration & Account Reconnaissance Playbook (IR-PLAYBOOK-003)
NIST Phase: Triage & Hardening | Category: Discovery
Summary: Guidance for assessing and countering systematic account discovery across identity directories.
Investigation Steps:
1. Collate the full list of distinct usernames tested by the remote host.
2. Cross-reference tested usernames against valid organizational employee and service account directories.
3. Determine if the adversary obtained an internal username list (e.g., from public LinkedIn scraping or prior breaches).
4. Assess whether the attacker switched to password spraying against the identified valid accounts.
Reference: MITRE D3FEND: D3-BAA (Biometric Authentication), D3-UD (User Account Disabling)

title: IR-PLAYBOOK-003: User Enumeration & Account Reconnaissance Playbook - Containment & Remediation
text:
Incident Response Playbook: User Enumeration & Account Reconnaissance Playbook (IR-PLAYBOOK-003) - Remediation Controls
Containment Actions:
1. Block or rate-limit the probing IP address.
2. Alert SOC monitoring team to flag future logins for any of the discovered valid usernames.
3. Verify that public login endpoints return generic error messages (e.g. 'Invalid credentials') that do not disclose whether a username exists.

Remediation Actions:
1. Remove default accounts (guest, test, demo, oracle) from systems.
2. Implement network access control lists (ACLs) to hide administrative interfaces from public internet exposure.
Reference: MITRE D3FEND: D3-BAA (Biometric Authentication), D3-UD (User Account Disabling)
